newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Investor faith in Russia recovers with Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Investor faith in Russia recovers with Yeltsin.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin's progress after heart surgery has given fresh confidence to foreign investors, and analysts said on Wednesday that Russian debt prices are on their way back to record highs.

"Russia is again a buy. The best possible outcome -- of a technocratic administration under the nominal control of a convalescent Yeltsin -- is now the base case," Bank of America analyst Richard Gray said.
The huge Russian debt market's immediate reaction to reports that Yeltsin was recovering well from his quintuple bypass surgery, was to send prices sharply higher to almost 80 cents in the dollar.

That is close to the record high of 82 cents seen early last month for the $32 billion worth of old Soviet foreign commercial debt, in the name of Vneshekonombank, which Moscow is close to restructuring by turning into long-term loans.
"I think we will go past the 82 (cents) peak," one European bank trader said.
With Yeltsin's operation out of the way, traders said they can now focus more on an apporaching Eurobond issue which Russia starts marketing to the international financial community next week.
The bond will be the first the Russian government has issued overseas in more than 80 years and is expected to be priced at 350 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
That compares to around 750-800 points for Vneshekonombank paper, which means prices are certain to head higher to get nearer to the Eurobond levels.
"There's no reason why prices shouldn't go back to the highs. We're bullish on the debt and equity marklet," chief East Europe economist and ING Barings, Philip Poole, said.

He expected the International Monetary Fund to release a delayed tranche of a loan on signs of improved tax collection in Russia, which has been a sore point in the country's efforts to transform into a market economy.
Paribas economist Stuart Brown warned that Yeltsin was not out of the woods yet and said the focus on his health underscored how fragile Russia's political system remained.
He added that while the longer-term outlook for higher prices was probably justified, there could well be volatility in the short-term.
